name: Devlin's Remains
summary: Devlin's Remains are the collected skeletal bones of Devlin Agamand, the younger son of the wealthy family who owned the Agamand Mills. Stalking the roads near his ruined ancestral estate as a mindless Scourge thrall, he was struck down to deliver his bones to a vengeful survivor in Brill.

sections.title: A Bitter Legacy
sections.body: In life, Devlin Agamand stood in the shadow of his elder brother Thurman. Where Thurman was gentle and tall, Devlin was remembered as physically frail and viciously sharp-tongued. When the Plague of Undeath swept through northern Tirisfal Glades, the Agamand family failed to protect their lands and laborers. Devlin was among the first to fall, reanimated as a ravenous Scourge ghoul whose frantic, mad chattering haunted the roadside leading up to Agamand Mills.

sections.title: Vengeance on the Mantle
sections.body: Coleman Farthing, a Forsaken residing in Brill, holds a deep and abiding grudge against the entire Agamand bloodline. Holding them directly responsible for failing his family when the plague arrived, Farthing tasked travelers with laying Devlin to rest and collecting his remains. Farthing sought to display Devlin's bones upon his mantle, savoring the knowledge that his former masters have been reduced to dust and shattered fragments under his heel.

faq.q: Who was Devlin Agamand in life?
faq.answer: Devlin was the younger son of the Agamand family, the wealthy landowners who built the Agamand Mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. Unlike his mild-tempered and broad-shouldered brother Thurman, Devlin was weak, sickly, and notoriously ill-tempered, known for a bitter and sharp tongue.

faq.q: Where were Devlin's remains gathered from?
faq.answer: They were taken from Devlin Agamand's Scourge-controlled corpse, located just south of the Agamand Mills along the road winding through Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: Why does Coleman Farthing want these bones?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing despises the Agamand family, believing they abandoned and failed him and his loved ones during the outbreak of the Plague. He intends to mount Devlin's bones on his mantelpiece in Brill as a trophy of vengeance and satisfaction.

faq.q: Is Devlin part of the Forsaken?
faq.answer: No. When Devlin succumbed to the Plague, his mind was lost entirely to the Scourge. He wandered the grounds near the mills as a mindless undead ghoul, babbling madness until destroyed.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, the Agamands represent the old, privileged nobility of Lordaeron whose failures left common folk to perish and rise as monsters, making the desecration of Devlin's remains an act of class retribution.
